(ID1484-022){{cite web |url=http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/kyushuyamaguchi/ky_yawata_01.html |title=The State-owned Yawata Steel Works |publisher=Kyuyama |access-date=17 February 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131016154751/http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/kyushuyamaguchi/ky_yawata_01.html |archive-date=16 October 2013 }} | establishing political decision was made in 1897, started operation in 1901, "Heritage of Industrial Modernization" by [[Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry|METI]]. | [[File:Governmental Yawata Iron & Steel Works.JPG|250px]] |- |rowspan="3" style="border-top:hidden"| |width="20%"| {{nihongo|The Imperial Steel Works: Office|八幡製鐵所 旧本事務所|Yahata seitetsusho kyū-jimusyo}} | constructed in 1899 | [[File:八幡製鉄所旧本事務所.JPG|250px]] |- |width="20%"| {{nihongo|The Imperial Steel Works: Repairing factory|八幡製鐵所 修繕工場|Yahata seitetsusho syūzen-kōjou}} | constructed in 1900, the oldest steel structure in Japan, still under operation. | |- |width="20%"| {{nihongo|The Imperial Steel Works: Metalsmith factory|八幡製鐵所 旧鍛冶工場|Yahata seitetsusho kyū-kaji-kōjou}} | constructed in 1900 | |- |colspan="2" | {{nihongo|Onga river Pumping Station|[[:ja:遠賀川水源地ポンプ室|遠賀川水源地ポンプ室]]|Onga-gawa suigenchi ponpu-shitsu}}
(ID1484-023) | constructed in 1910, still under operation. |[[File:遠賀川水源地ポンプ室１.JPG|250px]] |- |} ==Controversy== {{Main|Hashima_Island#World Heritage Site approval controversy}} The inclusion of some of these properties as UNESCO Heritage sites arraised concerns and objections from [[South Korea]], on the grounds that conscripted Korean civilians and Chinese prisoners-of-war were forced to work under harsh conditions at seven of these sites during Japan's [[World War II]] mobilization policies. There is a research questioning about Japanese government's compliance with UNESCO regulations and requirements with respect to Hashima Coal Mine site.{{cite journal |last=Palmer |first=David |date=January 1, 2018 |title=Gunkanjima / Battleship Island, Nagasaki: World Heritage Historical Site or Urban Ruins Tourist Attraction? |url=https://apjjf.org/2018/01/Palmer.html |journal=The Asia-Pacific Journal: Japan Focus |volume=16 |issue=1 |access-date=July 4, 2020}} Although the period at which forced labour took place does not coincide with the period of Meiji industrial revolution, the criticism arose based on the view that the Meiji industrial revolution was "inseparable from 20th-century empire-building, which led inexorably to Japanese colonialism and the Asia-Pacific War".{{cite news | title = Story of Japan's industrial rise deserves to be told, forced labor and all | url=https://www.japantimes.co.jp/community/2015/06/24/voices/story-japans-industrial-rise-deserves-told-forced-labor/ | access-date=2020-07-05 | work=The Japan Times | date=2015-06-24}} South Korea claimed that the official recognition of those sites would "violate the dignity of the survivors of forced labor as well as the spirit and principles of the UNESCO Convention", and "World Heritage sites should be of outstanding universal value and be acceptable by all peoples across the globe." China also released a similar statement that "World Heritage application should live up to the principle and spirit of promoting peace as upheld by UNESCO." ==See also== * [[World Heritage Sites in Japan]] * [[Hidden Christian Sites in the Nagasaki Region]] ==References== {{Reflist|2}} ==External links== * [https://whc.unesco.org/en/tentativelists/5399/ UNESCO Tentative List entry] * [http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/index.html The Modern Industrial Heritage Sites in Kyushu and Yamaguchi] * [http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/action/teigensyoE.pdf Emergence of Industrial Japan: Kyushu and Yamaguchi] * [http://www.kyuyama.jp/ The Modern Industrial Heritage Sites in Kyushu and Yamaguchi] {{in lang|ja}} * [https://www.ihic.jp/ Industrial Heritage Information Center] {{in lang|ja}} {{Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining}} {{World Heritage Sites in Japan}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Pages and Categories from Wikipedia 2]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:Anti-Japanese sentiment in Korea]] [[Category:Bakumatsu]] [[Category:Meiji period]] [[Category:Fukuoka Prefecture]] [[Category:Kagoshima Prefecture]] [[Category:Kumamoto Prefecture]] [[Category:Nagasaki Prefecture]] [[Category:Saga Prefecture]] [[Category:Yamaguchi Prefecture]] [[Category:Industrial archaeology]] [[Category:World Heritage Sites in Japan]] [[Category:Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:Pages and Categories from Wikipedia]] }} [[sn:Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining]] [[en:Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Modern Industrial Heritage Sites in Kyushu and Yamaguchi}} [[Category:New]]

{{Short description|UNESCO World Heritage Site in Japan}} {{Infobox UNESCO World Heritage Site | image = Hagi Castle Town Aerial photograph.1976.jpg | image_upright = 1.2 | caption = Aerial photograph of [[Hagi Castle]] Town | location = [[Japan]] | includes = | criteria = {{UNESCO WHS type|(ii), (iv)}}(ii), (iv) | ID = 1484 | coordinates = {{coord|34|25|50|N|131|24|44|E|display=title, inline|format=dms}} | year = 2015 | area = {{convert|306.66|ha|acre|abbr=on}} | buffer_zone = {{convert|2,408.33|ha|acre|abbr=on}} | locmapin = World | map_caption = }} {{nihongo|'''Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining'''|明治日本の産業革命遺産 製鉄・鉄鋼、造船、石炭産業|Meiji nihon no sangyōkakumei isan: seitetsu, tekkō, zōsen, sekitan sangyō}} are a group of historic sites that played an important part in the industrialization of [[Japan]] in the [[Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji (era)|Meiji]] periods (1850s–1910), and are part of the [[industrial heritage]] of Japan.{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1484/|title=Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining |publisher=[[UNESCO]] |access-date=5 July 2015}} In 2009 the monuments were submitted jointly for inscription on the [[UNESCO]] [[World Heritage List]] under criteria [[World Heritage Site#Cultural criteria|ii, iii, and iv]]. The sites were accepted at the 39th UNESCO World Heritage session, under the condition to take measures "that allow an understanding that there were a large number of Koreans and others who were brought against their will and forced to work under harsh conditions ...", and again, such measures have yet to be implemented.{{cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fZ5lR7Cj5C8| title=Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution, "Unfulfilled Promises" | website=[[YouTube]] }} Eight areas are registered, with twenty-three component sites:{{cn|date=July 2020}} ==Area 1: Hagi in Yamaguchi== Hagi proto-industrial sites and [[Tokugawa period]] cultural setting; [[Hagi, Yamaguchi|Hagi]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]]: {| class="wikitable sortable" width="100%" style="background:#ffffff;" |- !width="40%" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" | Site !width="40%" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" class="unsortable"| Comments !width="20%" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" class="unsortable"| image |- | {{nihongo|[[Hagi Reverberatory Furnace]]|萩反射炉|Hagi hansharo}}
(ID1484-001){{cite web |url=http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/kyushuyamaguchi/ky_hagi_01.html |title=Hagi Reverberatory Furnace |publisher=Kyuyama |access-date=17 February 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131016154643/http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/kyushuyamaguchi/ky_hagi_01.html |archive-date=16 October 2013 }}{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2373 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191210192707/https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2373 |archive-date=10 December 2019 |title=萩反射炉 |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=17 February 2012 }} || [[Monuments of Japan|Historic Site]] || [[File:Hagi Reverberatory furnaces.JPG|250px]] |- | {{nihongo|[[Ebisugahana Shipyard]]|恵美須ヶ鼻造船所跡|Ebisugahana zōsensho ato}}
(ID1484-002){{cite web |url=http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/kyushuyamaguchi/ky_hagi_02.html |title=Ebisugahana shipyard & Ohitayama-Tatara iron smelting works |publisher=Kyuyama |access-date=17 February 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131016154548/http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/kyushuyamaguchi/ky_hagi_02.html |archive-date=16 October 2013 }} || [[Monuments of Japan|Historic Site]] || [[File:Heisin_Maru.jpg|250px]] |- | {{nihongo|[[Ohitayama Tatara Iron Works]]|大板山たたら製鉄遺跡|Ōitayama tatara seitetsui ato}}
(ID1484-003){{cite web |url=http://bunkazai.ysn21.jp/bunkazai/detail.asp?mid=100031&pid=bl |title=大板山たたら製鉄遺跡 |publisher=[[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] |access-date=17 February 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120910022327/http://bunkazai.ysn21.jp/bunkazai/detail.asp?mid=100031&pid=bl |archive-date=10 September 2012 }} || [[Cultural Properties of Japan|Prefectural]] [[Monuments of Japan|Historic Site]] || [[File:Ohitayama-tatara Iron Works 04 Smelter.JPG|250px]] |- | {{nihongo|[[Hagi Castle|Hagi castle]] town|[[:ja:萩城下町|萩城下町]]|Hagi jōkamachi}}

(ID1484-005){{cite web |url=http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/kyushuyamaguchi/ky_hagi_04.html |title=The Shokasonjuku Academy |publisher=Kyuyama |access-date=17 February 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131016154748/http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/kyushuyamaguchi/ky_hagi_04.html |archive-date=16 October 2013 }}{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2366 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191210192426/https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2366 |archive-date=10 December 2019 |title=松下村塾 |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=17 February 2012 }} || run by [[Yoshida Shōin]]; [[Monuments of Japan|Historic Site]] || [[File:松下村塾.jpg|250px]] |- |} ==Area 2: Kagoshima== Shūseikan pioneering factory complex; [[Kagoshima, Kagoshima|Kagoshima]], [[Kagoshima Prefecture]]: {| class="wikitable sortable" width="100%" style="background:#ffffff;" |- !colspan="2" width="40%" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" | Site !width="40%" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" class="unsortable"| Comments !width="20" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" class="unsortable"| image |- |colspan="2" width="40%" | {{nihongo|Former Shūseikan|[[:ja:尚古集成館|旧集成館]]|kyū Shūseikan}}

(ID1484-010){{cite web |url=http://www5.pref.iwate.jp/~hp0252/hashino/history.html |title=橋野鉄鉱山の歴史 |trans-title=The history of Hashino iron mining and smelting site|website=[[Iwate Prefecture]] |access-date=June 2, 2020 }} || influenced Yawata (see below); [[Monuments of Japan|Historic Site]] || [[File:Hashino-sanbankouroato.jpg|250px]] |- |} ==Area 5: Saga== Mietsu shipyard; [[Saga, Saga|Saga]], [[Saga Prefecture]]: {| class="wikitable sortable" width="100%" style="background:#ffffff;" |- !width="40%" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" | Site !width="40%" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" class="unsortable"| Comments !width="20" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" class="unsortable"| image |- | {{nihongo|Mietsu Naval Dock|[[:ja:三重津海軍所|三重津海軍所跡]]|Mietsu kaigunsho ato}} (ID1484-011) {{cite web |url=https://mietsu-sekaiisan.jp/en/ |title=Mietsu Naval Dock |website=[[Saga Prefecture]] |access-date=June 2, 2020 }} || constructed in 1858, [[Monuments of Japan|Historic Site]] ||[[File:Mietsu Naval Dock view south.JPG|250px]] |- |} ==Area 6: Nagasaki== Nagasaki shipyard facilities, coal mining islands and associated sites; [[Nagasaki]], [[Nagasaki Prefecture]]: {| class="wikitable sortable" width="100%" style="background:#ffffff;" |- !width="40%" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" | Site !width="40%" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" class="unsortable"| Comments !width="20" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" class="unsortable"| image |- | {{nihongo|[[Kosuge Slip Dock]]|小菅修船場跡|Kosuge shūsenba ato}}

(ID1484-022){{cite web |url=http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/kyushuyamaguchi/ky_yawata_01.html |title=The State-owned Yawata Steel Works |publisher=Kyuyama |access-date=17 February 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131016154751/http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/kyushuyamaguchi/ky_yawata_01.html |archive-date=16 October 2013 }} | establishing political decision was made in 1897, started operation in 1901, "Heritage of Industrial Modernization" by [[Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry|METI]]. | [[File:Governmental Yawata Iron & Steel Works.JPG|250px]] |- |rowspan="3" style="border-top:hidden"| |width="20%"| {{nihongo|The Imperial Steel Works: Office|八幡製鐵所 旧本事務所|Yahata seitetsusho kyū-jimusyo}} | constructed in 1899 | [[File:八幡製鉄所旧本事務所.JPG|250px]] |- |width="20%"| {{nihongo|The Imperial Steel Works: Repairing factory|八幡製鐵所 修繕工場|Yahata seitetsusho syūzen-kōjou}} | constructed in 1900, the oldest steel structure in Japan, still under operation. | |- |width="20%"| {{nihongo|The Imperial Steel Works: Metalsmith factory|八幡製鐵所 旧鍛冶工場|Yahata seitetsusho kyū-kaji-kōjou}} | constructed in 1900 | |- |colspan="2" | {{nihongo|Onga river Pumping Station|[[:ja:遠賀川水源地ポンプ室|遠賀川水源地ポンプ室]]|Onga-gawa suigenchi ponpu-shitsu}}
(ID1484-023) | constructed in 1910, still under operation. |[[File:遠賀川水源地ポンプ室１.JPG|250px]] |- |} ==Controversy== {{Main|Hashima_Island#World Heritage Site approval controversy}} The inclusion of some of these properties as UNESCO Heritage sites arraised concerns and objections from [[South Korea]], on the grounds that conscripted Korean civilians and Chinese prisoners-of-war were forced to work under harsh conditions at seven of these sites during Japan's [[World War II]] mobilization policies. There is a research questioning about Japanese government's compliance with UNESCO regulations and requirements with respect to Hashima Coal Mine site.{{cite journal |last=Palmer |first=David |date=January 1, 2018 |title=Gunkanjima / Battleship Island, Nagasaki: World Heritage Historical Site or Urban Ruins Tourist Attraction? |url=https://apjjf.org/2018/01/Palmer.html |journal=The Asia-Pacific Journal: Japan Focus |volume=16 |issue=1 |access-date=July 4, 2020}} Although the period at which forced labour took place does not coincide with the period of Meiji industrial revolution, the criticism arose based on the view that the Meiji industrial revolution was "inseparable from 20th-century empire-building, which led inexorably to Japanese colonialism and the Asia-Pacific War".{{cite news | title = Story of Japan's industrial rise deserves to be told, forced labor and all | url=https://www.japantimes.co.jp/community/2015/06/24/voices/story-japans-industrial-rise-deserves-told-forced-labor/ | access-date=2020-07-05 | work=The Japan Times | date=2015-06-24}} South Korea claimed that the official recognition of those sites would "violate the dignity of the survivors of forced labor as well as the spirit and principles of the UNESCO Convention", and "World Heritage sites should be of outstanding universal value and be acceptable by all peoples across the globe." China also released a similar statement that "World Heritage application should live up to the principle and spirit of promoting peace as upheld by UNESCO." ==See also== * [[World Heritage Sites in Japan]] * [[Hidden Christian Sites in the Nagasaki Region]] ==References== {{Reflist|2}} ==External links== * [https://whc.unesco.org/en/tentativelists/5399/ UNESCO Tentative List entry] * [http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/index.html The Modern Industrial Heritage Sites in Kyushu and Yamaguchi] * [http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/action/teigensyoE.pdf Emergence of Industrial Japan: Kyushu and Yamaguchi] * [http://www.kyuyama.jp/ The Modern Industrial Heritage Sites in Kyushu and Yamaguchi] {{in lang|ja}} * [https://www.ihic.jp/ Industrial Heritage Information Center] {{in lang|ja}} {{Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining}} {{World Heritage Sites in Japan}} {{draft categories| }} {{draft categories| [[Category:Pages and Categories from Wikipedia 2]] [[Category:qq]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:Anti-Japanese sentiment in Korea]] [[Category:Bakumatsu]] [[Category:Meiji period]] [[Category:Fukuoka Prefecture]] [[Category:Kagoshima Prefecture]] [[Category:Kumamoto Prefecture]] [[Category:Nagasaki Prefecture]] [[Category:Saga Prefecture]] [[Category:Yamaguchi Prefecture]] [[Category:Industrial archaeology]] [[Category:World Heritage Sites in Japan]] [[Category:Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:Pages and Categories from Wikipedia]] }} [[sn:Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining]] [[en:Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Modern Industrial Heritage Sites in Kyushu and Yamaguchi}}

{{Short description|UNESCO World Heritage Site in Japan}} {{Infobox UNESCO World Heritage Site | image = Hagi Castle Town Aerial photograph.1976.jpg | image_upright = 1.2 | caption = Aerial photograph of [[Hagi Castle]] Town | location = [[Japan]] | includes = | criteria = {{UNESCO WHS type|(ii), (iv)}}(ii), (iv) | ID = 1484 | coordinates = {{coord|34|25|50|N|131|24|44|E|display=title, inline|format=dms}} | year = 2015 | area = {{convert|306.66|ha|acre|abbr=on}} | buffer_zone = {{convert|2,408.33|ha|acre|abbr=on}} | locmapin = World | map_caption = }} {{nihongo|'''Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining'''|明治日本の産業革命遺産 製鉄・鉄鋼、造船、石炭産業|Meiji nihon no sangyōkakumei isan: seitetsu, tekkō, zōsen, sekitan sangyō}} are a group of historic sites that played an important part in the industrialization of [[Japan]] in the [[Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji (era)|Meiji]] periods (1850s–1910), and are part of the [[industrial heritage]] of Japan.{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1484/|title=Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining |publisher=[[UNESCO]] |access-date=5 July 2015}} In 2009 the monuments were submitted jointly for inscription on the [[UNESCO]] [[World Heritage List]] under criteria [[World Heritage Site#Cultural criteria|ii, iii, and iv]]. The sites were accepted at the 39th UNESCO World Heritage session, under the condition to take measures "that allow an understanding that there were a large number of Koreans and others who were brought against their will and forced to work under harsh conditions ...", and again, such measures have yet to be implemented.{{cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fZ5lR7Cj5C8| title=Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution, "Unfulfilled Promises" | website=[[YouTube]] }} Eight areas are registered, with twenty-three component sites:{{cn|date=July 2020}} ==Area 1: Hagi in Yamaguchi== Hagi proto-industrial sites and [[Tokugawa period]] cultural setting; [[Hagi, Yamaguchi|Hagi]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]]: {| class="wikitable sortable" width="100%" style="background:#ffffff;" |- !width="40%" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" | Site !width="40%" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" class="unsortable"| Comments !width="20%" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" class="unsortable"| image |- | {{nihongo|[[Hagi Reverberatory Furnace]]|萩反射炉|Hagi hansharo}}

(ID1484-002){{cite web |url=http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/kyushuyamaguchi/ky_hagi_02.html |title=Ebisugahana shipyard & Ohitayama-Tatara iron smelting works |publisher=Kyuyama |access-date=17 February 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131016154548/http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/kyushuyamaguchi/ky_hagi_02.html |archive-date=16 October 2013 }} || [[Monuments of Japan|Historic Site]] || [[File:Heisin_Maru.jpg|250px]] |- | {{nihongo|[[Ohitayama Tatara Iron Works]]|大板山たたら製鉄遺跡|Ōitayama tatara seitetsui ato}}

(ID1484-005){{cite web |url=http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/kyushuyamaguchi/ky_hagi_04.html |title=The Shokasonjuku Academy |publisher=Kyuyama |access-date=17 February 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131016154748/http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/kyushuyamaguchi/ky_hagi_04.html |archive-date=16 October 2013 }}{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2366 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191210192426/https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2366 |archive-date=10 December 2019 |title=松下村塾 |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=17 February 2012 }} || run by [[Yoshida Shōin]]; [[Monuments of Japan|Historic Site]] || [[File:松下村塾.jpg|250px]] |- |} ==Area 2: Kagoshima== Shūseikan pioneering factory complex; [[Kagoshima, Kagoshima|Kagoshima]], [[Kagoshima Prefecture]]: {| class="wikitable sortable" width="100%" style="background:#ffffff;" |- !colspan="2" width="40%" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" | Site !width="40%" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" class="unsortable"| Comments !width="20" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" class="unsortable"| image |- |colspan="2" width="40%" | {{nihongo|Former Shūseikan|[[:ja:尚古集成館|旧集成館]]|kyū Shūseikan}}

(ID1484-008) | constructed in 1852 | |- |} ==Area 3: Nirayama in Shizuoka== Nirayama proto-industrial reverberatory furnace; [[Izunokuni, Shizuoka|Izunokuni]], [[Shizuoka Prefecture]]: {| class="wikitable sortable" width="100%" style="background:#ffffff;" |- !width="40%" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" | Site !width="40%" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" class="unsortable"| Comments !width="20%" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" class="unsortable"| image |- | {{nihongo|[[Nirayama Reverberatory Furnace]]|韮山反射炉|Niirayama hansharo}}

(ID1484-019){{cite web |url=http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/kyushuyamaguchi/ky_nagasaki_04.html |title=Former Glover House |publisher=Kyuyama |access-date=17 February 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131016154056/http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/kyushuyamaguchi/ky_nagasaki_04.html |archive-date=16 October 2013 }}{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/3527 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191223154802/https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/3527 |archive-date=23 December 2019 |title=旧グラバー住宅(長崎県長崎市南山手町) |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=17 February 2012 }} || erected in 1863; [[Important Cultural Properties of Japan|Important Cultural Property]] || [[File:Glover Garden 04.jpg|250px]] |- |} ==Area 7: Miike in Fukuoka and Kumamoto== Miike coal mines, railway and ports; [[Ōmuta, Fukuoka|Ōmuta]], [[Fukuoka Prefecture]], [[Arao, Kumamoto|Arao]] and [[Uki, Kumamoto|Uki]], [[Kumamoto Prefecture]]: {| class="wikitable sortable" width="100%" style="background:#ffffff;" |- !colspan="2" width="40%" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" | Site !width="40%" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" class="unsortable"| Comments !width="20" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" class="unsortable"| image |- |colspan="2" width="40%" | {{nihongo|[[Miike Coal Mine]] and Miike Port|[[:ja:三井三池炭鉱|三池炭鉱]]、[[:ja:三池港|三池港]]|Miike tankō, Miike-kō}}

extended to Miike Port in 1905, [[Important Cultural Properties of Japan|Important Cultural Property]] || [[File:Miike map circa 1930.PNG|250px]] |- |width="20%"| {{nihongo|Miike Port|三池港|Miike-kō}} Port|[[:ja:三角港|三角西港]]|Misumi nishi-kō}}

(ID1484-022){{cite web |url=http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/kyushuyamaguchi/ky_yawata_01.html |title=The State-owned Yawata Steel Works |publisher=Kyuyama |access-date=17 February 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131016154751/http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/kyushuyamaguchi/ky_yawata_01.html |archive-date=16 October 2013 }} | establishing political decision was made in 1897, started operation in 1901, "Heritage of Industrial Modernization" by [[Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry|METI]]. | [[File:Governmental Yawata Iron & Steel Works.JPG|250px]] |- |rowspan="3" style="border-top:hidden"| |width="20%"| {{nihongo|The Imperial Steel Works: Office|八幡製鐵所 旧本事務所|Yahata seitetsusho kyū-jimusyo}} | constructed in 1899 | [[File:八幡製鉄所旧本事務所.JPG|250px]] |- |width="20%"| {{nihongo|The Imperial Steel Works: Repairing factory|八幡製鐵所 修繕工場|Yahata seitetsusho syūzen-kōjou}} | constructed in 1900, the oldest steel structure in Japan, still under operation. | |- |width="20%"| {{nihongo|The Imperial Steel Works: Metalsmith factory|八幡製鐵所 旧鍛冶工場|Yahata seitetsusho kyū-kaji-kōjou}} | constructed in 1900 | |- |colspan="2" | {{nihongo|Onga river Pumping Station|[[:ja:遠賀川水源地ポンプ室|遠賀川水源地ポンプ室]]|Onga-gawa suigenchi ponpu-shitsu}}
(ID1484-023) | constructed in 1910, still under operation. |[[File:遠賀川水源地ポンプ室１.JPG|250px]] |- |} ==Controversy== {{Main|Hashima_Island#World Heritage Site approval controversy}} The inclusion of some of these properties as UNESCO Heritage sites arraised concerns and objections from [[South Korea]], on the grounds that conscripted Korean civilians and Chinese prisoners-of-war were forced to work under harsh conditions at seven of these sites during Japan's [[World War II]] mobilization policies. There is a research questioning about Japanese government's compliance with UNESCO regulations and requirements with respect to Hashima Coal Mine site.{{cite journal |last=Palmer |first=David |date=January 1, 2018 |title=Gunkanjima / Battleship Island, Nagasaki: World Heritage Historical Site or Urban Ruins Tourist Attraction? |url=https://apjjf.org/2018/01/Palmer.html |journal=The Asia-Pacific Journal: Japan Focus |volume=16 |issue=1 |access-date=July 4, 2020}} Although the period at which forced labour took place does not coincide with the period of Meiji industrial revolution, the criticism arose based on the view that the Meiji industrial revolution was "inseparable from 20th-century empire-building, which led inexorably to Japanese colonialism and the Asia-Pacific War".{{cite news | title = Story of Japan's industrial rise deserves to be told, forced labor and all | url=https://www.japantimes.co.jp/community/2015/06/24/voices/story-japans-industrial-rise-deserves-told-forced-labor/ | access-date=2020-07-05 | work=The Japan Times | date=2015-06-24}} South Korea claimed that the official recognition of those sites would "violate the dignity of the survivors of forced labor as well as the spirit and principles of the UNESCO Convention", and "World Heritage sites should be of outstanding universal value and be acceptable by all peoples across the globe." China also released a similar statement that "World Heritage application should live up to the principle and spirit of promoting peace as upheld by UNESCO." ==See also== * [[World Heritage Sites in Japan]] * [[Hidden Christian Sites in the Nagasaki Region]] ==References== {{Reflist|2}} ==External links== * [https://whc.unesco.org/en/tentativelists/5399/ UNESCO Tentative List entry] * [http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/index.html The Modern Industrial Heritage Sites in Kyushu and Yamaguchi] * [http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/action/teigensyoE.pdf Emergence of Industrial Japan: Kyushu and Yamaguchi] * [http://www.kyuyama.jp/ The Modern Industrial Heritage Sites in Kyushu and Yamaguchi] {{in lang|ja}} * [https://www.ihic.jp/ Industrial Heritage Information Center] {{in lang|ja}} {{Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining}} {{World Heritage Sites in Japan}} {{draft categories| }} {{draft categories| [[Category:Pages and Categories from Wikipedia 2]] [[Category:qq]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:Anti-Japanese sentiment in Korea]] [[Category:Bakumatsu]] [[Category:Meiji period]] [[Category:Fukuoka Prefecture]] [[Category:Kagoshima Prefecture]] [[Category:Kumamoto Prefecture]] [[Category:Nagasaki Prefecture]] [[Category:Saga Prefecture]] [[Category:Yamaguchi Prefecture]] [[Category:Industrial archaeology]] [[Category:World Heritage Sites in Japan]] [[Category:Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining]] [[Category:Pages and Categories from Wikipedia]] }} [[sn:Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining]] [[en:Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Modern Industrial Heritage Sites in Kyushu and Yamaguchi}}

{{Short description|UNESCO World Heritage Site in Japan}} {{Infobox UNESCO World Heritage Site | image = Hagi Castle Town Aerial photograph.1976.jpg | image_upright = 1.2 | caption = Aerial photograph of [[Hagi Castle]] Town | location = [[Japan]] | includes = | criteria = {{UNESCO WHS type|(ii), (iv)}}(ii), (iv) | ID = 1484 | coordinates = {{coord|34|25|50|N|131|24|44|E|display=title, inline|format=dms}} | year = 2015 | area = {{convert|306.66|ha|acre|abbr=on}} | buffer_zone = {{convert|2,408.33|ha|acre|abbr=on}} | locmapin = World | map_caption = }} {{nihongo|'''Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining'''|明治日本の産業革命遺産 製鉄・鉄鋼、造船、石炭産業|Meiji nihon no sangyōkakumei isan: seitetsu, tekkō, zōsen, sekitan sangyō}} are a group of historic sites that played an important part in the industrialization of [[Japan]] in the [[Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji (era)|Meiji]] periods (1850s–1910), and are part of the [[industrial heritage]] of Japan.{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1484/|title=Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining |publisher=[[UNESCO]] |access-date=5 July 2015}} In 2009 the monuments were submitted jointly for inscription on the [[UNESCO]] [[World Heritage List]] under criteria [[World Heritage Site#Cultural criteria|ii, iii, and iv]]. The sites were accepted at the 39th UNESCO World Heritage session, under the condition to take measures "that allow an understanding that there were a large number of Koreans and others who were brought against their will and forced to work under harsh conditions ...", and again, such measures have yet to be implemented.{{cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fZ5lR7Cj5C8| title=Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution, "Unfulfilled Promises" | website=[[YouTube]] }} Eight areas are registered, with twenty-three component sites:{{cn|date=July 2020}} ==Area 1: Hagi in Yamaguchi== Hagi proto-industrial sites and [[Tokugawa period]] cultural setting; [[Hagi, Yamaguchi|Hagi]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]]: {| class="wikitable sortable" width="100%" style="background:#ffffff;" |- !width="40%" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" | Site !width="40%" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" class="unsortable"| Comments !width="20%" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" class="unsortable"| image |- | {{nihongo|[[Hagi Reverberatory Furnace]]|萩反射炉|Hagi hansharo}}
(ID1484-001){{cite web |url=http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/kyushuyamaguchi/ky_hagi_01.html |title=Hagi Reverberatory Furnace |publisher=Kyuyama |access-date=17 February 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131016154643/http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/kyushuyamaguchi/ky_hagi_01.html |archive-date=16 October 2013 }}{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2373 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191210192707/https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2373 |archive-date=10 December 2019 |title=萩反射炉 |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=17 February 2012 }} || [[Monuments of Japan|Historic Site]] || [[File:Hagi Reverberatory furnaces.JPG|250px]] |- | {{nihongo|[[Ebisugahana Shipyard]]|恵美須ヶ鼻造船所跡|Ebisugahana zōsensho ato}}
(ID1484-002){{cite web |url=http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/kyushuyamaguchi/ky_hagi_02.html |title=Ebisugahana shipyard & Ohitayama-Tatara iron smelting works |publisher=Kyuyama |access-date=17 February 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131016154548/http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/kyushuyamaguchi/ky_hagi_02.html |archive-date=16 October 2013 }} || [[Monuments of Japan|Historic Site]] || [[File:Heisin_Maru.jpg|250px]] |- | {{nihongo|[[Ohitayama Tatara Iron Works]]|大板山たたら製鉄遺跡|Ōitayama tatara seitetsui ato}}
(ID1484-003){{cite web |url=http://bunkazai.ysn21.jp/bunkazai/detail.asp?mid=100031&pid=bl |title=大板山たたら製鉄遺跡 |publisher=[[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] |access-date=17 February 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120910022327/http://bunkazai.ysn21.jp/bunkazai/detail.asp?mid=100031&pid=bl |archive-date=10 September 2012 }} || [[Cultural Properties of Japan|Prefectural]] [[Monuments of Japan|Historic Site]] || [[File:Ohitayama-tatara Iron Works 04 Smelter.JPG|250px]] |- | {{nihongo|[[Hagi Castle|Hagi castle]] town|[[:ja:萩城下町|萩城下町]]|Hagi jōkamachi}}

(ID1484-023) | constructed in 1910, still under operation. |[[File:遠賀川水源地ポンプ室１.JPG|250px]] |- |} ==Controversy== {{Main|Hashima_Island#World Heritage Site approval controversy}} The inclusion of some of these properties as UNESCO Heritage sites arraised concerns and objections from [[South Korea]], on the grounds that conscripted Korean civilians and Chinese prisoners-of-war were forced to work under harsh conditions at seven of these sites during Japan's [[World War II]] mobilization policies. There is a research questioning about Japanese government's compliance with UNESCO regulations and requirements with respect to Hashima Coal Mine site.{{cite journal |last=Palmer |first=David |date=January 1, 2018 |title=Gunkanjima / Battleship Island, Nagasaki: World Heritage Historical Site or Urban Ruins Tourist Attraction? |url=https://apjjf.org/2018/01/Palmer.html |journal=The Asia-Pacific Journal: Japan Focus |volume=16 |issue=1 |access-date=July 4, 2020}} Although the period at which forced labour took place does not coincide with the period of Meiji industrial revolution, the criticism arose based on the view that the Meiji industrial revolution was "inseparable from 20th-century empire-building, which led inexorably to Japanese colonialism and the Asia-Pacific War".{{cite news | title = Story of Japan's industrial rise deserves to be told, forced labor and all | url=https://www.japantimes.co.jp/community/2015/06/24/voices/story-japans-industrial-rise-deserves-told-forced-labor/ | access-date=2020-07-05 | work=The Japan Times | date=2015-06-24}} South Korea claimed that the official recognition of those sites would "violate the dignity of the survivors of forced labor as well as the spirit and principles of the UNESCO Convention", and "World Heritage sites should be of outstanding universal value and be acceptable by all peoples across the globe." China also released a similar statement that "World Heritage application should live up to the principle and spirit of promoting peace as upheld by UNESCO." ==See also== * [[World Heritage Sites in Japan]] * [[Hidden Christian Sites in the Nagasaki Region]] ==References== {{Reflist|2}} ==External links== * [https://whc.unesco.org/en/tentativelists/5399/ UNESCO Tentative List entry] * [http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/index.html The Modern Industrial Heritage Sites in Kyushu and Yamaguchi] * [http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/action/teigensyoE.pdf Emergence of Industrial Japan: Kyushu and Yamaguchi] * [http://www.kyuyama.jp/ The Modern Industrial Heritage Sites in Kyushu and Yamaguchi] {{in lang|ja}} * [https://www.ihic.jp/ Industrial Heritage Information Center] {{in lang|ja}} {{Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining}} {{World Heritage Sites in Japan}} {{draft categories| }} {{draft categories| [[Category:Pages and Categories from Wikipedia 2]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:Anti-Japanese sentiment in Korea]] [[Category:Bakumatsu]] [[Category:Meiji period]] [[Category:Fukuoka Prefecture]] [[Category:Kagoshima Prefecture]] [[Category:Kumamoto Prefecture]] [[Category:Nagasaki Prefecture]] [[Category:Saga Prefecture]] [[Category:Yamaguchi Prefecture]] [[Category:Industrial archaeology]] [[Category:World Heritage Sites in Japan]] [[Category:Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining]] [[Category:Pages and Categories from Wikipedia]] }} [[sn:Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining]] [[en:Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Modern Industrial Heritage Sites in Kyushu and Yamaguchi}}

{{Short description|UNESCO World Heritage Site in Japan}} {{Infobox UNESCO World Heritage Site | image = Hagi Castle Town Aerial photograph.1976.jpg | image_upright = 1.2 | caption = Aerial photograph of [[Hagi Castle]] Town | location = [[Japan]] | includes = | criteria = {{UNESCO WHS type|(ii), (iv)}}(ii), (iv) | ID = 1484 | coordinates = {{coord|34|25|50|N|131|24|44|E|display=title, inline|format=dms}} | year = 2015 | area = {{convert|306.66|ha|acre|abbr=on}} | buffer_zone = {{convert|2,408.33|ha|acre|abbr=on}} | locmapin = World | map_caption = }} {{nihongo|'''Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining'''|明治日本の産業革命遺産 製鉄・鉄鋼、造船、石炭産業|Meiji nihon no sangyōkakumei isan: seitetsu, tekkō, zōsen, sekitan sangyō}} are a group of historic sites that played an important part in the industrialization of [[Japan]] in the [[Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji (era)|Meiji]] periods (1850s–1910), and are part of the [[industrial heritage]] of Japan.{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1484/|title=Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining |publisher=[[UNESCO]] |access-date=5 July 2015}} In 2009 the monuments were submitted jointly for inscription on the [[UNESCO]] [[World Heritage List]] under criteria [[World Heritage Site#Cultural criteria|ii, iii, and iv]]. The sites were accepted at the 39th UNESCO World Heritage session, under the condition to take measures "that allow an understanding that there were a large number of Koreans and others who were brought against their will and forced to work under harsh conditions ...", and again, such measures have yet to be implemented.{{cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fZ5lR7Cj5C8| title=Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution, "Unfulfilled Promises" | website=[[YouTube]] }} Eight areas are registered, with twenty-three component sites:{{cn|date=July 2020}} ==Area 1: Hagi in Yamaguchi== Hagi proto-industrial sites and [[Tokugawa period]] cultural setting; [[Hagi, Yamaguchi|Hagi]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]]: {| class="wikitable sortable" width="100%" style="background:#ffffff;" |- !width="40%" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" | Site !width="40%" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" class="unsortable"| Comments !width="20%" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" class="unsortable"| image |- | {{nihongo|[[Hagi Reverberatory Furnace]]|萩反射炉|Hagi hansharo}}

(ID1484-022){{cite web |url=http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/kyushuyamaguchi/ky_yawata_01.html |title=The State-owned Yawata Steel Works |publisher=Kyuyama |access-date=17 February 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131016154751/http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/kyushuyamaguchi/ky_yawata_01.html |archive-date=16 October 2013 }} | establishing political decision was made in 1897, started operation in 1901, "Heritage of Industrial Modernization" by [[Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry|METI]]. | [[File:Governmental Yawata Iron & Steel Works.JPG|250px]] |- |rowspan="3" style="border-top:hidden"| |width="20%"| {{nihongo|The Imperial Steel Works: Office|八幡製鐵所 旧本事務所|Yahata seitetsusho kyū-jimusyo}} | constructed in 1899 | [[File:八幡製鉄所旧本事務所.JPG|250px]] |- |width="20%"| {{nihongo|The Imperial Steel Works: Repairing factory|八幡製鐵所 修繕工場|Yahata seitetsusho syūzen-kōjou}} | constructed in 1900, the oldest steel structure in Japan, still under operation. | |- |width="20%"| {{nihongo|The Imperial Steel Works: Metalsmith factory|八幡製鐵所 旧鍛冶工場|Yahata seitetsusho kyū-kaji-kōjou}} | constructed in 1900 | |- |colspan="2" | {{nihongo|Onga river Pumping Station|[[:ja:遠賀川水源地ポンプ室|遠賀川水源地ポンプ室]]|Onga-gawa suigenchi ponpu-shitsu}}
(ID1484-023) | constructed in 1910, still under operation. |[[File:遠賀川水源地ポンプ室１.JPG|250px]] |- |} ==Controversy== {{Main|Hashima_Island#World Heritage Site approval controversy}} The inclusion of some of these properties as UNESCO Heritage sites arraised concerns and objections from [[South Korea]], on the grounds that conscripted Korean civilians and Chinese prisoners-of-war were forced to work under harsh conditions at seven of these sites during Japan's [[World War II]] mobilization policies. There is a research questioning about Japanese government's compliance with UNESCO regulations and requirements with respect to Hashima Coal Mine site.{{cite journal |last=Palmer |first=David |date=January 1, 2018 |title=Gunkanjima / Battleship Island, Nagasaki: World Heritage Historical Site or Urban Ruins Tourist Attraction? |url=https://apjjf.org/2018/01/Palmer.html |journal=The Asia-Pacific Journal: Japan Focus |volume=16 |issue=1 |access-date=July 4, 2020}} Although the period at which forced labour took place does not coincide with the period of Meiji industrial revolution, the criticism arose based on the view that the Meiji industrial revolution was "inseparable from 20th-century empire-building, which led inexorably to Japanese colonialism and the Asia-Pacific War".{{cite news | title = Story of Japan's industrial rise deserves to be told, forced labor and all | url=https://www.japantimes.co.jp/community/2015/06/24/voices/story-japans-industrial-rise-deserves-told-forced-labor/ | access-date=2020-07-05 | work=The Japan Times | date=2015-06-24}} South Korea claimed that the official recognition of those sites would "violate the dignity of the survivors of forced labor as well as the spirit and principles of the UNESCO Convention", and "World Heritage sites should be of outstanding universal value and be acceptable by all peoples across the globe." China also released a similar statement that "World Heritage application should live up to the principle and spirit of promoting peace as upheld by UNESCO." ==See also== * [[World Heritage Sites in Japan]] * [[Hidden Christian Sites in the Nagasaki Region]] ==References== {{Reflist|2}} ==External links== * [https://whc.unesco.org/en/tentativelists/5399/ UNESCO Tentative List entry] * [http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/index.html The Modern Industrial Heritage Sites in Kyushu and Yamaguchi] * [http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/action/teigensyoE.pdf Emergence of Industrial Japan: Kyushu and Yamaguchi] * [http://www.kyuyama.jp/ The Modern Industrial Heritage Sites in Kyushu and Yamaguchi] {{in lang|ja}} * [https://www.ihic.jp/ Industrial Heritage Information Center] {{in lang|ja}} {{Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining}} {{World Heritage Sites in Japan}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Modern Industrial Heritage Sites in Kyushu and Yamaguchi}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Pages and Categories from Wikipedia 2]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:Anti-Japanese sentiment in Korea]] [[Category:Bakumatsu]] [[Category:Meiji period]] [[Category:Fukuoka Prefecture]] [[Category:Kagoshima Prefecture]] [[Category:Kumamoto Prefecture]] [[Category:Nagasaki Prefecture]] [[Category:Saga Prefecture]] [[Category:Yamaguchi Prefecture]] [[Category:Industrial archaeology]] [[Category:World Heritage Sites in Japan]] [[Category:Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining]] [[Category:Pages and Categories from Wikipedia]] }} [[sn:Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining]] [[en:Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining]]

{{Short description|UNESCO World Heritage Site in Japan}} {{Infobox UNESCO World Heritage Site | image = Hagi Castle Town Aerial photograph.1976.jpg | image_upright = 1.2 | caption = Aerial photograph of [[Hagi Castle]] Town | location = [[Japan]] | includes = | criteria = {{UNESCO WHS type|(ii), (iv)}}(ii), (iv) | ID = 1484 | coordinates = {{coord|34|25|50|N|131|24|44|E|display=title, inline|format=dms}} | year = 2015 | area = {{convert|306.66|ha|acre|abbr=on}} | buffer_zone = {{convert|2,408.33|ha|acre|abbr=on}} | locmapin = World | map_caption = }} {{nihongo|'''Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining'''|明治日本の産業革命遺産 製鉄・鉄鋼、造船、石炭産業|Meiji nihon no sangyōkakumei isan: seitetsu, tekkō, zōsen, sekitan sangyō}} are a group of historic sites that played an important part in the industrialization of [[Japan]] in the [[Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji (era)|Meiji]] periods (1850s–1910), and are part of the [[industrial heritage]] of Japan.{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1484/|title=Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining |publisher=[[UNESCO]] |access-date=5 July 2015}} In 2009 the monuments were submitted jointly for inscription on the [[UNESCO]] [[World Heritage List]] under criteria [[World Heritage Site#Cultural criteria|ii, iii, and iv]]. The sites were accepted at the 39th UNESCO World Heritage session, under the condition to take measures "that allow an understanding that there were a large number of Koreans and others who were brought against their will and forced to work under harsh conditions ...", and again, such measures have yet to be implemented.{{cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fZ5lR7Cj5C8| title=Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution, "Unfulfilled Promises" | website=[[YouTube]] }} Eight areas are registered, with twenty-three component sites:{{cn|date=July 2020}} ==Area 1: Hagi in Yamaguchi== Hagi proto-industrial sites and [[Tokugawa period]] cultural setting; [[Hagi, Yamaguchi|Hagi]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]]: {| class="wikitable sortable" width="100%" style="background:#ffffff;" |- !width="40%" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" | Site !width="40%" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" class="unsortable"| Comments !width="20%" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" class="unsortable"| image |- | {{nihongo|[[Hagi Reverberatory Furnace]]|萩反射炉|Hagi hansharo}}

(ID1484-003){{cite web |url=http://bunkazai.ysn21.jp/bunkazai/detail.asp?mid=100031&pid=bl |title=大板山たたら製鉄遺跡 |publisher=[[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] |access-date=17 February 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120910022327/http://bunkazai.ysn21.jp/bunkazai/detail.asp?mid=100031&pid=bl |archive-date=10 September 2012 }} || [[Cultural Properties of Japan|Prefectural]] [[Monuments of Japan|Historic Site]] || [[File:Ohitayama-tatara Iron Works 04 Smelter.JPG|250px]] |- | {{nihongo|[[Hagi Castle|Hagi castle]] town|[[:ja:萩城下町|萩城下町]]|Hagi jōkamachi}}

(ID1484-005){{cite web |url=http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/kyushuyamaguchi/ky_hagi_04.html |title=The Shokasonjuku Academy |publisher=Kyuyama |access-date=17 February 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131016154748/http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/kyushuyamaguchi/ky_hagi_04.html |archive-date=16 October 2013 }}{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2366 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191210192426/https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2366 |archive-date=10 December 2019 |title=松下村塾 |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=17 February 2012 }} || run by [[Yoshida Shōin]]; [[Monuments of Japan|Historic Site]] || [[File:松下村塾.jpg|250px]] |- |} ==Area 2: Kagoshima== Shūseikan pioneering factory complex; [[Kagoshima, Kagoshima|Kagoshima]], [[Kagoshima Prefecture]]: {| class="wikitable sortable" width="100%" style="background:#ffffff;" |- !colspan="2" width="40%" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" | Site !width="40%" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" class="unsortable"| Comments !width="20" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" class="unsortable"| image |- |colspan="2" width="40%" | {{nihongo|Former Shūseikan|[[:ja:尚古集成館|旧集成館]]|kyū Shūseikan}}

(ID1484-022){{cite web |url=http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/kyushuyamaguchi/ky_yawata_01.html |title=The State-owned Yawata Steel Works |publisher=Kyuyama |access-date=17 February 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131016154751/http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/kyushuyamaguchi/ky_yawata_01.html |archive-date=16 October 2013 }} | establishing political decision was made in 1897, started operation in 1901, "Heritage of Industrial Modernization" by [[Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry|METI]]. | [[File:Governmental Yawata Iron & Steel Works.JPG|250px]] |- |rowspan="3" style="border-top:hidden"| |width="20%"| {{nihongo|The Imperial Steel Works: Office|八幡製鐵所 旧本事務所|Yahata seitetsusho kyū-jimusyo}} | constructed in 1899 | [[File:八幡製鉄所旧本事務所.JPG|250px]] |- |width="20%"| {{nihongo|The Imperial Steel Works: Repairing factory|八幡製鐵所 修繕工場|Yahata seitetsusho syūzen-kōjou}} | constructed in 1900, the oldest steel structure in Japan, still under operation. | |- |width="20%"| {{nihongo|The Imperial Steel Works: Metalsmith factory|八幡製鐵所 旧鍛冶工場|Yahata seitetsusho kyū-kaji-kōjou}} | constructed in 1900 | |- |colspan="2" | {{nihongo|Onga river Pumping Station|[[:ja:遠賀川水源地ポンプ室|遠賀川水源地ポンプ室]]|Onga-gawa suigenchi ponpu-shitsu}}
(ID1484-023) | constructed in 1910, still under operation. |[[File:遠賀川水源地ポンプ室１.JPG|250px]] |- |} ==Controversy== {{Main|Hashima_Island#World Heritage Site approval controversy}} The inclusion of some of these properties as UNESCO Heritage sites arraised concerns and objections from [[South Korea]], on the grounds that conscripted Korean civilians and Chinese prisoners-of-war were forced to work under harsh conditions at seven of these sites during Japan's [[World War II]] mobilization policies. There is a research questioning about Japanese government's compliance with UNESCO regulations and requirements with respect to Hashima Coal Mine site.{{cite journal |last=Palmer |first=David |date=January 1, 2018 |title=Gunkanjima / Battleship Island, Nagasaki: World Heritage Historical Site or Urban Ruins Tourist Attraction? |url=https://apjjf.org/2018/01/Palmer.html |journal=The Asia-Pacific Journal: Japan Focus |volume=16 |issue=1 |access-date=July 4, 2020}} Although the period at which forced labour took place does not coincide with the period of Meiji industrial revolution, the criticism arose based on the view that the Meiji industrial revolution was "inseparable from 20th-century empire-building, which led inexorably to Japanese colonialism and the Asia-Pacific War".{{cite news | title = Story of Japan's industrial rise deserves to be told, forced labor and all | url=https://www.japantimes.co.jp/community/2015/06/24/voices/story-japans-industrial-rise-deserves-told-forced-labor/ | access-date=2020-07-05 | work=The Japan Times | date=2015-06-24}} South Korea claimed that the official recognition of those sites would "violate the dignity of the survivors of forced labor as well as the spirit and principles of the UNESCO Convention", and "World Heritage sites should be of outstanding universal value and be acceptable by all peoples across the globe." China also released a similar statement that "World Heritage application should live up to the principle and spirit of promoting peace as upheld by UNESCO." ==See also== * [[World Heritage Sites in Japan]] * [[Hidden Christian Sites in the Nagasaki Region]] ==References== {{Reflist|2}} ==External links== * [https://whc.unesco.org/en/tentativelists/5399/ UNESCO Tentative List entry] * [http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/index.html The Modern Industrial Heritage Sites in Kyushu and Yamaguchi] * [http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/action/teigensyoE.pdf Emergence of Industrial Japan: Kyushu and Yamaguchi] * [http://www.kyuyama.jp/ The Modern Industrial Heritage Sites in Kyushu and Yamaguchi] {{in lang|ja}} * [https://www.ihic.jp/ Industrial Heritage Information Center] {{in lang|ja}} {{Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining}} {{World Heritage Sites in Japan}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Pages and Categories from Wikipedia 2]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:Anti-Japanese sentiment in Korea]] [[Category:Bakumatsu]] [[Category:Meiji period]] [[Category:Fukuoka Prefecture]] [[Category:Kagoshima Prefecture]] [[Category:Kumamoto Prefecture]] [[Category:Nagasaki Prefecture]] [[Category:Saga Prefecture]] [[Category:Yamaguchi Prefecture]] [[Category:Industrial archaeology]] [[Category:World Heritage Sites in Japan]] [[Category:Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining]] [[Category:Pages and Categories from Wikipedia]] }} [[sn:Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining]] [[en:Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining]]

{{Short description|UNESCO World Heritage Site in Japan}} {{Infobox UNESCO World Heritage Site | image = Hagi Castle Town Aerial photograph.1976.jpg | image_upright = 1.2 | caption = Aerial photograph of [[Hagi Castle]] Town | location = [[Japan]] | includes = | criteria = {{UNESCO WHS type|(ii), (iv)}}(ii), (iv) | ID = 1484 | coordinates = {{coord|34|25|50|N|131|24|44|E|display=title, inline|format=dms}} | year = 2015 | area = {{convert|306.66|ha|acre|abbr=on}} | buffer_zone = {{convert|2,408.33|ha|acre|abbr=on}} | locmapin = World | map_caption = }} {{nihongo|'''Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining'''|明治日本の産業革命遺産 製鉄・鉄鋼、造船、石炭産業|Meiji nihon no sangyōkakumei isan: seitetsu, tekkō, zōsen, sekitan sangyō}} are a group of historic sites that played an important part in the industrialization of [[Japan]] in the [[Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji (era)|Meiji]] periods (1850s–1910), and are part of the [[industrial heritage]] of Japan.{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1484/|title=Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining |publisher=[[UNESCO]] |access-date=5 July 2015}} In 2009 the monuments were submitted jointly for inscription on the [[UNESCO]] [[World Heritage List]] under criteria [[World Heritage Site#Cultural criteria|ii, iii, and iv]]. The sites were accepted at the 39th UNESCO World Heritage session, under the condition to take measures "that allow an understanding that there were a large number of Koreans and others who were brought against their will and forced to work under harsh conditions ...", and again, such measures have yet to be implemented.{{cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fZ5lR7Cj5C8| title=Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution, "Unfulfilled Promises" | website=[[YouTube]] }} Eight areas are registered, with twenty-three component sites:{{cn|date=July 2020}} ==Area 1: Hagi in Yamaguchi== Hagi proto-industrial sites and [[Tokugawa period]] cultural setting; [[Hagi, Yamaguchi|Hagi]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]]: {| class="wikitable sortable" width="100%" style="background:#ffffff;" |- !width="40%" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" | Site !width="40%" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" class="unsortable"| Comments !width="20%" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" class="unsortable"| image |- | {{nihongo|[[Hagi Reverberatory Furnace]]|萩反射炉|Hagi hansharo}}

(ID1484-003){{cite web |url=http://bunkazai.ysn21.jp/bunkazai/detail.asp?mid=100031&pid=bl |title=大板山たたら製鉄遺跡 |publisher=[[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] |access-date=17 February 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120910022327/http://bunkazai.ysn21.jp/bunkazai/detail.asp?mid=100031&pid=bl |archive-date=10 September 2012 }} || [[Cultural Properties of Japan|Prefectural]] [[Monuments of Japan|Historic Site]] || [[File:Ohitayama-tatara Iron Works 04 Smelter.JPG|250px]] |- | {{nihongo|[[Hagi Castle|Hagi castle]] town|[[:ja:萩城下町|萩城下町]]|Hagi jōkamachi}}

(ID1484-005){{cite web |url=http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/kyushuyamaguchi/ky_hagi_04.html |title=The Shokasonjuku Academy |publisher=Kyuyama |access-date=17 February 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131016154748/http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/kyushuyamaguchi/ky_hagi_04.html |archive-date=16 October 2013 }}{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2366 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191210192426/https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2366 |archive-date=10 December 2019 |title=松下村塾 |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=17 February 2012 }} || run by [[Yoshida Shōin]]; [[Monuments of Japan|Historic Site]] || [[File:松下村塾.jpg|250px]] |- |} ==Area 2: Kagoshima== Shūseikan pioneering factory complex; [[Kagoshima, Kagoshima|Kagoshima]], [[Kagoshima Prefecture]]: {| class="wikitable sortable" width="100%" style="background:#ffffff;" |- !colspan="2" width="40%" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" | Site !width="40%" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" class="unsortable"| Comments !width="20" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" class="unsortable"| image |- |colspan="2" width="40%" | {{nihongo|Former Shūseikan|[[:ja:尚古集成館|旧集成館]]|kyū Shūseikan}}

(ID1484-023) | constructed in 1910, still under operation. |[[File:遠賀川水源地ポンプ室１.JPG|250px]] |- |} ==Controversy== {{Main|Hashima_Island#World Heritage Site approval controversy}} The inclusion of some of these properties as UNESCO Heritage sites arraised concerns and objections from [[South Korea]], on the grounds that conscripted Korean civilians and Chinese prisoners-of-war were forced to work under harsh conditions at seven of these sites during Japan's [[World War II]] mobilization policies. There is a research questioning about Japanese government's compliance with UNESCO regulations and requirements with respect to Hashima Coal Mine site.{{cite journal |last=Palmer |first=David |date=January 1, 2018 |title=Gunkanjima / Battleship Island, Nagasaki: World Heritage Historical Site or Urban Ruins Tourist Attraction? |url=https://apjjf.org/2018/01/Palmer.html |journal=The Asia-Pacific Journal: Japan Focus |volume=16 |issue=1 |access-date=July 4, 2020}} Although the period at which forced labour took place does not coincide with the period of Meiji industrial revolution, the criticism arose based on the view that the Meiji industrial revolution was "inseparable from 20th-century empire-building, which led inexorably to Japanese colonialism and the Asia-Pacific War".{{cite news | title = Story of Japan's industrial rise deserves to be told, forced labor and all | url=https://www.japantimes.co.jp/community/2015/06/24/voices/story-japans-industrial-rise-deserves-told-forced-labor/ | access-date=2020-07-05 | work=The Japan Times | date=2015-06-24}} South Korea claimed that the official recognition of those sites would "violate the dignity of the survivors of forced labor as well as the spirit and principles of the UNESCO Convention", and "World Heritage sites should be of outstanding universal value and be acceptable by all peoples across the globe." China also released a similar statement that "World Heritage application should live up to the principle and spirit of promoting peace as upheld by UNESCO." ==See also== * [[World Heritage Sites in Japan]] * [[Hidden Christian Sites in the Nagasaki Region]] ==References== {{Reflist|2}} ==External links== * [https://whc.unesco.org/en/tentativelists/5399/ UNESCO Tentative List entry] * [http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/index.html The Modern Industrial Heritage Sites in Kyushu and Yamaguchi] * [http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/action/teigensyoE.pdf Emergence of Industrial Japan: Kyushu and Yamaguchi] * [http://www.kyuyama.jp/ The Modern Industrial Heritage Sites in Kyushu and Yamaguchi] {{in lang|ja}} * [https://www.ihic.jp/ Industrial Heritage Information Center] {{in lang|ja}} {{Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining}} {{World Heritage Sites in Japan}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Pages and Categories from Wikipedia 2]] [[Category:Anti-Japanese sentiment in Korea]] [[Category:Bakumatsu]] [[Category:Meiji period]] [[Category:Fukuoka Prefecture]] [[Category:Kagoshima Prefecture]] [[Category:Kumamoto Prefecture]] [[Category:Nagasaki Prefecture]] [[Category:Saga Prefecture]] [[Category:Yamaguchi Prefecture]] [[Category:Industrial archaeology]] [[Category:World Heritage Sites in Japan]] [[Category:Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining]] [[Category:Pages and Categories from Wikipedia]] }} [[sn:Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining]] [[en:Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining]]

{{Short description|UNESCO World Heritage Site in Japan}} {{Infobox UNESCO World Heritage Site | image = Hagi Castle Town Aerial photograph.1976.jpg | image_upright = 1.2 | caption = Aerial photograph of [[Hagi Castle]] Town | location = [[Japan]] | includes = | criteria = {{UNESCO WHS type|(ii), (iv)}}(ii), (iv) | ID = 1484 | coordinates = {{coord|34|25|50|N|131|24|44|E|display=title, inline|format=dms}} | year = 2015 | area = {{convert|306.66|ha|acre|abbr=on}} | buffer_zone = {{convert|2,408.33|ha|acre|abbr=on}} | locmapin = World | map_caption = }} {{nihongo|'''Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining'''|明治日本の産業革命遺産 製鉄・鉄鋼、造船、石炭産業|Meiji nihon no sangyōkakumei isan: seitetsu, tekkō, zōsen, sekitan sangyō}} are a group of historic sites that played an important part in the industrialization of [[Japan]] in the [[Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji (era)|Meiji]] periods (1850s–1910), and are part of the [[industrial heritage]] of Japan.{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1484/|title=Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining |publisher=[[UNESCO]] |access-date=5 July 2015}} In 2009 the monuments were submitted jointly for inscription on the [[UNESCO]] [[World Heritage List]] under criteria [[World Heritage Site#Cultural criteria|ii, iii, and iv]]. The sites were accepted at the 39th UNESCO World Heritage session, under the condition to take measures "that allow an understanding that there were a large number of Koreans and others who were brought against their will and forced to work under harsh conditions ...", and again, such measures have yet to be implemented.{{cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fZ5lR7Cj5C8| title=Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution, "Unfulfilled Promises" | website=[[YouTube]] }} Eight areas are registered, with twenty-three component sites:{{cn|date=July 2020}} ==Area 1: Hagi in Yamaguchi== Hagi proto-industrial sites and [[Tokugawa period]] cultural setting; [[Hagi, Yamaguchi|Hagi]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]]: {| class="wikitable sortable" width="100%" style="background:#ffffff;" |- !width="40%" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" | Site !width="40%" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" class="unsortable"| Comments !width="20%" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" class="unsortable"| image |- | {{nihongo|[[Hagi Reverberatory Furnace]]|萩反射炉|Hagi hansharo}}

(ID1484-002){{cite web |url=http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/kyushuyamaguchi/ky_hagi_02.html |title=Ebisugahana shipyard & Ohitayama-Tatara iron smelting works |publisher=Kyuyama |access-date=17 February 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131016154548/http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/kyushuyamaguchi/ky_hagi_02.html |archive-date=16 October 2013 }} || [[Monuments of Japan|Historic Site]] || [[File:Heisin_Maru.jpg|250px]] |- | {{nihongo|[[Ohitayama Tatara Iron Works]]|大板山たたら製鉄遺跡|Ōitayama tatara seitetsui ato}}
(ID1484-003){{cite web |url=http://bunkazai.ysn21.jp/bunkazai/detail.asp?mid=100031&pid=bl |title=大板山たたら製鉄遺跡 |publisher=[[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] |access-date=17 February 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120910022327/http://bunkazai.ysn21.jp/bunkazai/detail.asp?mid=100031&pid=bl |archive-date=10 September 2012 }} || [[Cultural Properties of Japan|Prefectural]] [[Monuments of Japan|Historic Site]] || [[File:Ohitayama-tatara Iron Works 04 Smelter.JPG|250px]] |- | {{nihongo|[[Hagi Castle|Hagi castle]] town|[[:ja:萩城下町|萩城下町]]|Hagi jōkamachi}}

(ID1484-023) | constructed in 1910, still under operation. |[[File:遠賀川水源地ポンプ室１.JPG|250px]] |- |} ==Controversy== {{Main|Hashima_Island#World Heritage Site approval controversy}} The inclusion of some of these properties as UNESCO Heritage sites arraised concerns and objections from [[South Korea]], on the grounds that conscripted Korean civilians and Chinese prisoners-of-war were forced to work under harsh conditions at seven of these sites during Japan's [[World War II]] mobilization policies. There is a research questioning about Japanese government's compliance with UNESCO regulations and requirements with respect to Hashima Coal Mine site.{{cite journal |last=Palmer |first=David |date=January 1, 2018 |title=Gunkanjima / Battleship Island, Nagasaki: World Heritage Historical Site or Urban Ruins Tourist Attraction? |url=https://apjjf.org/2018/01/Palmer.html |journal=The Asia-Pacific Journal: Japan Focus |volume=16 |issue=1 |access-date=July 4, 2020}} Although the period at which forced labour took place does not coincide with the period of Meiji industrial revolution, the criticism arose based on the view that the Meiji industrial revolution was "inseparable from 20th-century empire-building, which led inexorably to Japanese colonialism and the Asia-Pacific War".{{cite news | title = Story of Japan's industrial rise deserves to be told, forced labor and all | url=https://www.japantimes.co.jp/community/2015/06/24/voices/story-japans-industrial-rise-deserves-told-forced-labor/ | access-date=2020-07-05 | work=The Japan Times | date=2015-06-24}} South Korea claimed that the official recognition of those sites would "violate the dignity of the survivors of forced labor as well as the spirit and principles of the UNESCO Convention", and "World Heritage sites should be of outstanding universal value and be acceptable by all peoples across the globe." China also released a similar statement that "World Heritage application should live up to the principle and spirit of promoting peace as upheld by UNESCO." ==See also== * [[World Heritage Sites in Japan]] * [[Hidden Christian Sites in the Nagasaki Region]] ==References== {{Reflist|2}} ==External links== * [https://whc.unesco.org/en/tentativelists/5399/ UNESCO Tentative List entry] * [http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/index.html The Modern Industrial Heritage Sites in Kyushu and Yamaguchi] * [http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/action/teigensyoE.pdf Emergence of Industrial Japan: Kyushu and Yamaguchi] * [http://www.kyuyama.jp/ The Modern Industrial Heritage Sites in Kyushu and Yamaguchi] {{in lang|ja}} * [https://www.ihic.jp/ Industrial Heritage Information Center] {{in lang|ja}} {{Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining}} {{World Heritage Sites in Japan}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Pages and Categories from Wikipedia 2]] [[Category:Anti-Japanese sentiment in Korea]] [[Category:Bakumatsu]] [[Category:Meiji period]] [[Category:Fukuoka Prefecture]] [[Category:Kagoshima Prefecture]] [[Category:Kumamoto Prefecture]] [[Category:Nagasaki Prefecture]] [[Category:Saga Prefecture]] [[Category:Yamaguchi Prefecture]] [[Category:World Heritage Sites in Japan]] [[Category:Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining]] [[Category:Pages and Categories from Wikipedia]] }} [[sn:Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining]] [[en:Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining]]

{{Short description|UNESCO World Heritage Site in Japan}} {{Infobox UNESCO World Heritage Site | image = Hagi Castle Town Aerial photograph.1976.jpg | image_upright = 1.2 | caption = Aerial photograph of [[Hagi Castle]] Town | location = [[Japan]] | includes = | criteria = {{UNESCO WHS type|(ii), (iv)}}(ii), (iv) | ID = 1484 | coordinates = {{coord|34|25|50|N|131|24|44|E|display=title, inline|format=dms}} | year = 2015 | area = {{convert|306.66|ha|acre|abbr=on}} | buffer_zone = {{convert|2,408.33|ha|acre|abbr=on}} | locmapin = World | map_caption = }} {{nihongo|'''Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining'''|明治日本の産業革命遺産 製鉄・鉄鋼、造船、石炭産業|Meiji nihon no sangyōkakumei isan: seitetsu, tekkō, zōsen, sekitan sangyō}} are a group of historic sites that played an important part in the industrialization of [[Japan]] in the [[Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji (era)|Meiji]] periods (1850s–1910), and are part of the [[industrial heritage]] of Japan.{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1484/|title=Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining |publisher=[[UNESCO]] |access-date=5 July 2015}} In 2009 the monuments were submitted jointly for inscription on the [[UNESCO]] [[World Heritage List]] under criteria [[World Heritage Site#Cultural criteria|ii, iii, and iv]]. The sites were accepted at the 39th UNESCO World Heritage session, under the condition to take measures "that allow an understanding that there were a large number of Koreans and others who were brought against their will and forced to work under harsh conditions ...", and again, such measures have yet to be implemented.{{cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fZ5lR7Cj5C8| title=Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution, "Unfulfilled Promises" | website=[[YouTube]] }} Eight areas are registered, with twenty-three component sites:{{cn|date=July 2020}} ==Area 1: Hagi in Yamaguchi== Hagi proto-industrial sites and [[Tokugawa period]] cultural setting; [[Hagi, Yamaguchi|Hagi]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]]: {| class="wikitable sortable" width="100%" style="background:#ffffff;" |- !width="40%" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" | Site !width="40%" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" class="unsortable"| Comments !width="20%" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" class="unsortable"| image |- | {{nihongo|[[Hagi Reverberatory Furnace]]|萩反射炉|Hagi hansharo}}

(ID1484-022){{cite web |url=http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/kyushuyamaguchi/ky_yawata_01.html |title=The State-owned Yawata Steel Works |publisher=Kyuyama |access-date=17 February 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131016154751/http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/kyushuyamaguchi/ky_yawata_01.html |archive-date=16 October 2013 }} | establishing political decision was made in 1897, started operation in 1901, "Heritage of Industrial Modernization" by [[Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry|METI]]. | [[File:Governmental Yawata Iron & Steel Works.JPG|250px]] |- |rowspan="3" style="border-top:hidden"| |width="20%"| {{nihongo|The Imperial Steel Works: Office|八幡製鐵所 旧本事務所|Yahata seitetsusho kyū-jimusyo}} | constructed in 1899 | [[File:八幡製鉄所旧本事務所.JPG|250px]] |- |width="20%"| {{nihongo|The Imperial Steel Works: Repairing factory|八幡製鐵所 修繕工場|Yahata seitetsusho syūzen-kōjou}} | constructed in 1900, the oldest steel structure in Japan, still under operation. | |- |width="20%"| {{nihongo|The Imperial Steel Works: Metalsmith factory|八幡製鐵所 旧鍛冶工場|Yahata seitetsusho kyū-kaji-kōjou}} | constructed in 1900 | |- |colspan="2" | {{nihongo|Onga river Pumping Station|[[:ja:遠賀川水源地ポンプ室|遠賀川水源地ポンプ室]]|Onga-gawa suigenchi ponpu-shitsu}}
(ID1484-023) | constructed in 1910, still under operation. |[[File:遠賀川水源地ポンプ室１.JPG|250px]] |- |} ==Controversy== {{Main|Hashima_Island#World Heritage Site approval controversy}} The inclusion of some of these properties as UNESCO Heritage sites arraised concerns and objections from [[South Korea]], on the grounds that conscripted Korean civilians and Chinese prisoners-of-war were forced to work under harsh conditions at seven of these sites during Japan's [[World War II]] mobilization policies. There is a research questioning about Japanese government's compliance with UNESCO regulations and requirements with respect to Hashima Coal Mine site.{{cite journal |last=Palmer |first=David |date=January 1, 2018 |title=Gunkanjima / Battleship Island, Nagasaki: World Heritage Historical Site or Urban Ruins Tourist Attraction? |url=https://apjjf.org/2018/01/Palmer.html |journal=The Asia-Pacific Journal: Japan Focus |volume=16 |issue=1 |access-date=July 4, 2020}} Although the period at which forced labour took place does not coincide with the period of Meiji industrial revolution, the criticism arose based on the view that the Meiji industrial revolution was "inseparable from 20th-century empire-building, which led inexorably to Japanese colonialism and the Asia-Pacific War".{{cite news | title = Story of Japan's industrial rise deserves to be told, forced labor and all | url=https://www.japantimes.co.jp/community/2015/06/24/voices/story-japans-industrial-rise-deserves-told-forced-labor/ | access-date=2020-07-05 | work=The Japan Times | date=2015-06-24}} South Korea claimed that the official recognition of those sites would "violate the dignity of the survivors of forced labor as well as the spirit and principles of the UNESCO Convention", and "World Heritage sites should be of outstanding universal value and be acceptable by all peoples across the globe." China also released a similar statement that "World Heritage application should live up to the principle and spirit of promoting peace as upheld by UNESCO." ==See also== * [[World Heritage Sites in Japan]] * [[Hidden Christian Sites in the Nagasaki Region]] ==References== {{Reflist|2}} ==External links== * [https://whc.unesco.org/en/tentativelists/5399/ UNESCO Tentative List entry] * [http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/index.html The Modern Industrial Heritage Sites in Kyushu and Yamaguchi] * [http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/action/teigensyoE.pdf Emergence of Industrial Japan: Kyushu and Yamaguchi] * [http://www.kyuyama.jp/ The Modern Industrial Heritage Sites in Kyushu and Yamaguchi] {{in lang|ja}} * [https://www.ihic.jp/ Industrial Heritage Information Center] {{in lang|ja}} {{Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining}} {{World Heritage Sites in Japan}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Pages and Categories from Wikipedia 2]] [[Category:Anti-Japanese sentiment in Korea]] [[Category:Bakumatsu]] [[Category:Meiji period]] [[Category:Fukuoka Prefecture]] [[Category:Kagoshima Prefecture]] [[Category:Kumamoto Prefecture]] [[Category:Nagasaki Prefecture]] [[Category:Saga Prefecture]] [[Category:Yamaguchi Prefecture]] [[Category:World Heritage Sites in Japan]] [[Category:Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining]] [[Category:Pages and Categories from Wikipedia]] }} [[sn:Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining]] [[en:Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining]] [[Category:Pages without translation templates]]

{{Short description|UNESCO World Heritage Site in Japan}} {{Infobox UNESCO World Heritage Site | image = Hagi Castle Town Aerial photograph.1976.jpg | image_upright = 1.2 | caption = Aerial photograph of [[Hagi Castle]] Town | location = [[Japan]] | includes = | criteria = {{UNESCO WHS type|(ii), (iv)}}(ii), (iv) | ID = 1484 | coordinates = {{coord|34|25|50|N|131|24|44|E|display=title, inline|format=dms}} | year = 2015 | area = {{convert|306.66|ha|acre|abbr=on}} | buffer_zone = {{convert|2,408.33|ha|acre|abbr=on}} | locmapin = World | map_caption = }} {{nihongo|'''Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining'''|明治日本の産業革命遺産 製鉄・鉄鋼、造船、石炭産業|Meiji nihon no sangyōkakumei isan: seitetsu, tekkō, zōsen, sekitan sangyō}} are a group of historic sites that played an important part in the industrialization of [[Japan]] in the [[Bakumatsu]] and [[Meiji (era)|Meiji]] periods (1850s–1910), and are part of the [[industrial heritage]] of Japan.{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1484/|title=Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining |publisher=[[UNESCO]] |access-date=5 July 2015}} In 2009 the monuments were submitted jointly for inscription on the [[UNESCO]] [[World Heritage List]] under criteria [[World Heritage Site#Cultural criteria|ii, iii, and iv]]. The sites were accepted at the 39th UNESCO World Heritage session, under the condition to take measures "that allow an understanding that there were a large number of Koreans and others who were brought against their will and forced to work under harsh conditions ...", and again, such measures have yet to be implemented.{{cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fZ5lR7Cj5C8| title=Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution, "Unfulfilled Promises" | website=[[YouTube]] }} Eight areas are registered, with twenty-three component sites:{{cn|date=July 2020}} ==Area 1: Hagi in Yamaguchi== Hagi proto-industrial sites and [[Tokugawa period]] cultural setting; [[Hagi, Yamaguchi|Hagi]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]]: {| class="wikitable sortable" width="100%" style="background:#ffffff;" |- !width="40%" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" | Site !width="40%" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" class="unsortable"| Comments !width="20%" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" class="unsortable"| image |- | {{nihongo|[[Hagi Reverberatory Furnace]]|萩反射炉|Hagi hansharo}}

(ID1484-005){{cite web |url=http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/kyushuyamaguchi/ky_hagi_04.html |title=The Shokasonjuku Academy |publisher=Kyuyama |access-date=17 February 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131016154748/http://www.kyuyama.jp/e/kyushuyamaguchi/ky_hagi_04.html |archive-date=16 October 2013 }}{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2366 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191210192426/https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2366 |archive-date=10 December 2019 |title=松下村塾 |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=17 February 2012 }} || run by [[Yoshida Shōin]]; [[Monuments of Japan|Historic Site]] || [[File:松下村塾.jpg|250px]] |- |} ==Area 2: Kagoshima== Shūseikan pioneering factory complex; [[Kagoshima, Kagoshima|Kagoshima]], [[Kagoshima Prefecture]]: {| class="wikitable sortable" width="100%" style="background:#ffffff;" |- !colspan="2" width="40%" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" | Site !width="40%" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" class="unsortable"| Comments !width="20" align="left" style="background:#ffdead;" class="unsortable"| image |- |colspan="2" width="40%" | {{nihongo|Former Shūseikan|[[:ja:尚古集成館|旧集成館]]|kyū Shūseikan}}
